subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement a default security boundary, keep it opt-in via `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandboxing, or introduce a versioned path-policy design before changing defaults?
rationale: The remaining work changes the security boundary and can break existing trusted-operator workflows, while partial file-tool fixes do not settle exec/process access.

options.title: Define the boundary first
options.body: Choose the default confinement, exec/process scope, migration behavior, and docs contract before merging partial PRs.

options.title: Land file-tool policy only
options.body: Treat file tools as the immediate boundary and keep exec/process isolation explicitly out of scope for a separate tracker.

options.title: Keep current opt-in model
options.body: Close or defer the default-boundary request and document sandboxing plus `tools.fs.workspaceOnly=true` as the supported answer.

recommendation.title: Define the boundary first
recommendation.body: Choose the default confinement, exec/process scope, migration behavior, and docs contract before merging partial PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current routing signal for the active filesystem policy and host tool code in this shallow checkout.
